hero.headline: City of Westlake expands homebuying program after surge in applications, raises purchase limit to $679,324
hero.teaser: A WPTV story about the City of Westlake's homebuying program sparked more than 200 inquiries, leading city leaders to expand eligibility and increase the home purchase limit.
hero.body:
A WPTV story about Westlake's Housing Assistance Purchase Program Yearly sparked more than 200 inquiries after airing in April, according to Taylor Garcia, the city's housing assistance program manager. Of those inquiries, 40 people submitted applications and 22 families were awarded assistance. The surge in interest prompted city leaders to expand the program to help even more families achieve homeownership.

On June 2, Westlake City Council approved major updates to the program. Buyers can now purchase a home up to $679,324, an increase from the previous limit of $568,577, to keep up with today's market. Instead of offering fixed amounts, the city now evaluates each family's financial situation to provide exactly what they need. The funds come as a 0% interest, forgivable loan that can be used for down payments, closing costs or buying down interest rates.

The program targets first-time homebuyers or those who haven't owned a home in three years. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, meet income limits, and buy a newly built home in Westlake under $679,324. Essential workers like police, firefighters, teachers and nurses can earn up to $300,000 and still qualify. Current Westlake residents and past program participants receive special consideration, and families can combine HAPPY money with other assistance programs to maximize their help.

The city is developing an online portal to streamline the application process. "A lot of families think homeownership is out of reach, but this program makes it possible," Garcia said. The expanded program reflects Westlake's commitment to helping families navigate the challenging housing market and establish roots in the community.

cards.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
cards.teaser: A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
cards.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane. FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a "death trap." Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said people don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and it's kind of a dangerous road sometimes. Townsend said everybody's always in a hurry and that living there makes him worry about young people learning to drive on that road because he has young kids. The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. Budensiek said in January that the question will be how many more people have to die before that project begins. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes.

cards.headline: FIFA lifts Folarin Balogun suspension after Trump calls president before U.S. World Cup match
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of the American striker, whose red-card suspension was lifted in time for Monday's World Cup match against Belgium in Seattle.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the United States' 2-0 round of 32 victory over Bosnia-Herzegovina on Wednesday, asking FIFA to review the red card given to striker Folarin Balogun, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity. FIFA announced Sunday that Balogun's automatic one-match suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match against Belgium on Monday. Brazilian referee Raphael Claus initially didn't signal a card but showed Balogun red after a video review in the 64th minute for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović. The decision appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. Trump posted on social media thanking FIFA for doing what was right and reversing a great injustice.

The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished by the decision and is investigating all potential options to safeguard the legitimate rights of all participating teams and protect the fundamental principles of fair play. Belgium coach Rudi Garcia said through a translator that he didn't know that in FIFA offices the fifth of July was the first of April in Europe, comparing it to April Fools' Day. Balogun leads the U.S. team with three goals in the tournament, matching Landon Donovan in 2010 for the second-most goals by an American in a World Cup. The 25-year-old plays for Monaco, where he scored 13 Ligue 1 goals last season.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce transforms Crain Estate into artistic destination
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the legacy of the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and international artists.
cards.body:
Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the non-profit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Many parts of the house look the same as when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room, which features man paneling, manly colors, stained glass, and leads out to a bar on the front patio. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The estate remains 90% the way it was when the Crains were there.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally. From the seven, there are now over 100. One peacock named Bob is believed to be 60 years old and is recognized by his limp. Bob lives inside and has his own bowls, with staff hand-feeding him daily. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Krystal Masters, the art director, leading one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners.

cards.headline: Westlake expands homebuying assistance program after surge in applications
cards.teaser: The City of Westlake received more than 200 inquiries and awarded assistance to 22 families after WPTV coverage of its HAPPY program in April.
cards.body:
A WPTV story about the City of Westlake homebuying program sparked a flood of applications, and now the city is making it even easier for first-time buyers to get help. Back in April, WPTV's Christy Waite introduced viewers to Westlake's Housing Assistance Purchase Program Yearly, known as HAPPY. Since the story aired, Westlake received more than 200 inquiries said Taylor Garcia, the city's housing assistance program manager. Of those, 40 people were able to submit applications, and 22 families were awarded assistance.

The surge in interest prompted city leaders to expand the program. On June 2, Westlake City Council approved major updates to help even more families. Instead of fixed amounts, the city now evaluates each family's financial situation to give them exactly what they need. Buyers can now purchase a home up to $679,324, up from $568,577, to keep up with today's market. The funds come as a 0% interest, forgivable loan that can be used for down payments, closing costs or buying down interest rates.

Current Westlake residents and past program participants get special consideration, and families can combine HAPPY money with other assistance programs to maximize their help. The city also told WPTV that an online portal is coming to streamline the process. To qualify, applicants must be first-time homebuyers or haven't owned a home in three years, be U.S. citizens, meet income limits, and buy a newly built home in Westlake under $679,324. Essential workers like police, firefighters, teachers and nurses can earn up to $300,000 and still qualify.

"A lot of families think homeownership is out of reach, but this program makes it possible," Garcia said. The program provides assistance through forgivable loans that help families overcome the financial barriers to purchasing their first home in the city's competitive real estate market.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes today for $3 million renovation to nearly double boat slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock closed July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock closed July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section to board passengers there. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and he hopes the project will add more floating docks. Kuyrkendall said the dock can get hectic on weekends when the company squeezes in trying to find spots.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there's a pretty significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city. He said this is a way for the city to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike. According to the FDOT website, the partial interchange is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiancée in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée, Misty Dawn White, in a deadly home fire earlier this week.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke exclusively about the loss and returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief. Fenn said she learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé, Mark, who told her that Misty had passed away in a fire.

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, having lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. White's birthday is July 4, making her death just a few days before her birthday particularly heartbreaking. Fenn said White has always been a good soul to her and will always be in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescues two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: The 44-year-old tennis star withdrew from her scheduled doubles match after fluid was drained from her knee following her singles return match earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old announced the decision on Instagram, writing that she was heartbroken to withdraw and that competing alongside Venus once more meant the world to her. She posted images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match and a video of her walking with strapping up and down her right leg while one of her daughters appeared to hold a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday in a three-set loss.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. The sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon. Serena indicated she could play again soon, telling fans to stay tuned to a city near them with the U.S. Open approaching. Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool.

cards.headline: Argentina beats Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina survived a challenge from Cape Verde in South Florida, advancing to face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a World Cup match that went to extra time, with the go-ahead goal credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the defense on a pass from Martinez and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, made 10 saves including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday in the Round of 16. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: New York Mets prospect selected for 2026 MLB Futures Game
cards.teaser: A lone Mets prospect received the honor to play in this year's Futures Game showcasing top minor league talent.
cards.body:
One New York Mets prospect was selected to participate in the 2026 MLB Futures Game, an annual showcase of top minor league players. The selection represents recognition for the prospect's performance in the Mets farm system this season.

The Futures Game provides an opportunity for prospects to compete against other top minor league talent and gain exposure on a national stage. The game features players from across all levels of the minor leagues who are considered among the top prospects in baseball.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are putting in summer work as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season with their sights set on a state title. The Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players, with the majority coming from the middle school program. Robertson said they know how things are run and have had a lot of success in their careers, and he hopes their senior year will be the best season the program has had.

With veteran senior leadership, the program is leaning into a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level with a challenging schedule because they want to compete against really good teams and attract new people. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting that going undefeated in the season does not matter if they keep losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, with players working harder so they can see positive results when the season starts and break team records.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce historic estate into arts destination
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists. Operating from the historic Crain Estate, the non-profit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility. "Jackson is the one who did all the tiling throughout the facility, and you'll see it from the ground to the walls to the ceiling," says Krystal Masters, the art director. The estate remains largely unchanged, staying 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there.

Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Many parts of the house look the same as when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with man paneling, manly colored bathroom, and stained glass that leads out to the bar on the front patio. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character without commercializing it.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds that have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable because he walks with a limp. "Bob usually typically lives in here. He is a very spoiled peacock as you can see he has his own bowls we hand feed him everyday," says Masters. Tour guides say peacocks feeding from children's hands create unforgettable moments. The Crains also once kept monkeys on the property after Jaxson Crain traveled to South America and returned with a baby monkey in his pocket.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab welcomes visitors of all skill levels with classes for children and adults. "The majority of my classes are one on one classes you come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art and it makes you feel good," Krystal said. The lab features various mediums and projects, including sculpting and watercolor workshops like paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow. "Art is a form of therapy and it distresses people………leave happy and haven't been on their phone scrolling," Krystal said.
